technologies.html.from: Instead of a long directory of individual tools, this page groups my experience into the technology domains I use to shape enterprise platforms, integrations, delivery environments and production operations.
technologies.html.to: My work spans the technology domains needed to shape enterprise platforms, connect systems, support delivery teams and keep production environments dependable.

technologies.html.from: Eight technology domains cover the stack I work across.
technologies.html.to: The stack is broad, but the decisions fall naturally into eight domains.

technologies.html.from: The grouping makes the portfolio easier to scan and better reflects how technology decisions are made in enterprise and healthcare environments.
technologies.html.to: These domains reflect how I actually work: choosing capabilities around the operating problem, the architecture and the responsibilities that continue after go-live.

technologies.html.from: I do not position myself as a specialist in 160 separate tools. I position the stack around the problems it solves.
technologies.html.to: The value is not in naming more tools. It is in combining the right capabilities around the problem.

technologies.html.from: The result is a clearer executive technology profile: architecture, healthcare interoperability, enterprise integration, application engineering, cloud/platform operations, data, infrastructure and delivery.
technologies.html.to: That is how I use architecture, healthcare interoperability, integration, engineering, cloud/platform operations, data and infrastructure as one connected technology practice.

architecture.html.from: My Solution Architecture approach connects business capability, solution boundaries, integration contracts, data responsibilities, non-functional requirements and operating ownership — so architecture remains useful from the first decision through go-live and stabilization.
architecture.html.to: I use architecture to turn a complex operating problem into decisions people can build, test, run and own — connecting business capability, system boundaries, integration contracts, data responsibilities and non-functional requirements from the start.

architecture.html.from: Good architecture reduces ambiguity before it becomes operational cost.
architecture.html.to: Good architecture makes hard decisions clearer before they become expensive in production.

architecture.html.from: That means clearer boundaries, cleaner contracts, fewer hidden assumptions and stronger ownership from design through production.
architecture.html.to: Clear boundaries, explicit contracts and visible ownership reduce the hidden assumptions that usually surface later as delivery friction or operational risk.
